The reply says sources conflict and calls the question unresolved, but it adds a "slight lean to Auer." The stated confidence is only 35. The reply does not settle on an answer. It leans toward B, though, and the instruction counts a lean as giving an answer "even if it adds a caveat."

The headline is "Unresolved," which points toward N. The parenthetical lean to Auer is a tentative preference, and the reply's explicit position is that the matter is unresolved. The criteria say N applies when the reply "says the answer is undetermined... or presents both without preferring either." Here it does express a preference, even a slight one, so it is not the case of "without preferring either." That makes B the better label.

B
